The core insight is that NFL play-calling exhibits two distinct temporal regimes: a high-performance script phase (first 15) followed by a degradation phase post-script. This is modeled via a Markov process where transitions depend on prior outcomes (shocks) and situational context. The serial correlation manifests as negative switching behavior after adverse events—e.g., after a sack, teams are more likely to continue rushing rather than switch to pass. This is captured through multinomial logistic regression with time-varying parameters. The kernel integrates these dynamics into a unified framework that explains both the emergence of predictable patterns and their eventual breakdown under pressure. The failure mode arises when coaches fail to adapt beyond the initial script, leading to overfitting to early-game tendencies.
